title: Wired 96-98% gaming keyboard, hot-swappable, 8 kHz, $60-120
no_credible_testing: No source on the brief's most-credible list (Consumer Reports, RTINGS, Which?, Wirecutter, Trusted Reviews, CPSC) has tested these boards. The finalists rest on hands-on reviews from established tech publications, tiered fair, plus manufacturer specs. Switch feel is a matter of taste and was not measured by anyone here.

sources.name: Tom's Hardware — Keychron V5 Ultra 8K review
Tom's Guide — Royal Kludge S98 review
Logitech G316 X 98 product page (manufacturer spec)
Keychron V5 Ultra 8K product page (manufacturer spec)
Lester Chan — G316 X owner review (personal blog)

finalists.name: Logitech G316 X 98
finalists.why: the only finalist with more than a handful of reviews — 121 on the maker's own store plus several hands-on press reviews
notes: TweakTown found the tactile version stiff on the larger keys and fairly loud
no switch or keycap puller in the box
TechRadar's main criticism was the lack of wireless

finalists.name: Keychron V5 8K
finalists.why: cheapest board that meets every requirement; the wired-only version of the V5 Ultra, so it shares its switches and features

specs.build: tray mount, steel plate, double-shot PBT keycaps, 1080 g

notes: a tray mount with a steel plate usually feels firmer than a gasket mount
almost no customer reviews yet, and no press review of this exact model

finalists.name: Keychron V5 Ultra 8K
finalists.why: the only finalist that keeps 8 kHz polling over wireless

specs.polling: 8000 Hz wired or wireless, ships set to 1000 Hz
specs.build: gasket mount, PC plate, double-shot PBT keycaps, 983 g, 660-hour battery
specs.reviews: 2 on keychron.com, plus a Tom's Hardware review

notes: Tom's Hardware calls it a solid option for a budget 8K board and praises battery life and comfort
ships at 1000 Hz — 8 kHz has to be switched on in Keychron's web app over a wired connection

choose_if.condition: you want to use it away from the desk, or without a cable, at any point
you would rather not be the first person to review a product you bought

ruled_out.name: Royal Kludge S98
ruled_out.why: hot-swappable with a tactile option, but 8 kHz is not advertised

ruled_out.name: RK C96 HE
ruled_out.why: 8 kHz and rapid trigger, but its magnetic switches are linear only

ruled_out.name: Corsair Vanguard 96
ruled_out.why: tactile and 8 kHz, but switches are soldered in, so not hot-swappable

caveats: US buyer; prices and availability differ elsewhere.
How each tactile switch feels is a matter of taste and no source here measured it. Keychron's Banana is reported to be lighter than its Brown.
The star ratings and fuller review detail on the Keychron boards could not be read.
Amazon and Best Buy are linked without prices on purpose — see decision 0003.
